column4: Identical camera, pose and coal-black background as the reference, but a white glove is being peeled down off this porcelain hand like a skin: the glove is turned inside out and bunched around the fingers, half off, the ball-jointed porcelain wrist and palm already bare. Five fingers. Clean closed outline, no text.

Same room and layout as the first reference. On the left, seen from behind over her shoulder: the living librarian from the second reference's back view, long loose orange hair with the orange flower and black ribbon, white long-sleeved blouse, layered black, ivory and orange skirt; she wears NO maid headband, NO apron and NO big white back bow. On the right, inside the tall mirror frame, stands a brand-new porcelain maid doll (third reference): white headband, black dress, white apron, ball joints and wrist rings, eyes open, facing her with the same face. No text.

Continue the reference: identical camera and the same black dressmaker shears, but the blades have just snapped fully shut. The thread bundle is cut clean through: the left half of the threads drops away down-left and the right half springs up and away to the upper right, short frayed ends curling in the air; a gap where they were joined. Flat empty ivory background. No hand, no text.

Continue the reference: identical camera, the same bare living hand and white cuff in the same pose, but the tan-gold string has slipped off completely and falls away down past the bottom edge, a loose curve with nothing holding it; the open hand is now empty and free. Flat ivory background. No text.
